question.worked_solution:
We need to remove the radical $\sqrt{49{r}^{5}}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{49{r}^{5}},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{16p}}{\sqrt{49{r}^{5}}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{16p}\cdot \sqrt{49{r}^{5}}}{\sqrt{49{r}^{5}}\cdot \sqrt{49{r}^{5}}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{16\cdot p}\cdot \sqrt{49{r}^{4}\cdot r}}{(\sqrt{49{r}^{5}})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{p}\cdot 7{r}^{2}\sqrt{r}}{49{r}^{5}} & = \\ \frac{28{r}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{pr}}{49{r}^{5}} & = \\ \frac{4\cdot \cancel{7{r}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{pr}}{7\cdot \cancel{7{r}^{2}}\cdot {r}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{4\sqrt{pr}}{7{r}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$
